We are pleased by how we closed out 2025. As I reflect on our full year results, our
advantages in product innovation, market leadership, platform, and scale enabled our
teams to manage the business well through a highly uncertain demand environment
and the impact of U.S. tariffs.

我們對2025年結尾感到滿意。隨着本人回顧我們的全年業績，我們在產品創新、市場領
導地位、平台以及規模上的優勢，使我們的團隊在需求高度不明朗的環境中及受美國關稅
的影響下妥善管理業務。




Kyle Gendreau
Chief Executive Officer 行政總裁

CORPORATE PROFILE
公司簡介

With a heritage dating back to 1910, Samsonite Group S.A. (together     新秀麗集團有限公司（連同其綜合附屬公司統稱
with its consolidated subsidiaries, the “Company,” the “Group,”         為「本公司」、「本集團」或「我們」）的歷史可追溯
“our,” “us” or “we”) is the world’s best-known and largest travel       至1910 年，是全球最著名、規模最大的行李箱公
luggage company and a leader in global lifestyle bags. We own           司，並且是全球時尚箱包行業的翹楚。我們擁有
and operate a portfolio of consumer-centric and iconic brands,          及經營以新秀麗 、TUMI 及American Tourister 為
led by Samsonite , TUMI , and American Tourister , that empower         首並以消費者為中心的標誌性品牌組合，該等品
our customers’ journeys with globally trusted, innovative and           牌為我們客戶的旅程提供全球信賴、創新及日益
increasingly sustainable products. Building on our long history of      可持續發展的產品。憑藉我們歷史悠久的行業領
industry leadership, our vision is to create a path toward a more       導地位，本公司的願景是引領行業邁向更可持續
sustainable future for our industry.                                    發展的未來。

    customers, vendors, and other stakeholders.                               之間的關係。

    employees and helps them to grow and thrive together.                     化。

    performance. See “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations – Adjusted Net Income” for a
    reconciliation from our profit attributable to equity holders to adjusted net income.
    經調整淨收入為非IFRS財務計量工具，其撇除影響我們呈報的股權持有人應佔溢利的多項成本、費用及貸項以及若干其他非現金費用（連同其各
    自的稅項影響）的影響，我們相信其有助證券分析員、投資者及其他利益相關方更全面了解我們的相關財務表現。有關我們股權持有人應佔溢利
    與經調整淨收入的對賬，請參閱財務狀況及經營業績的管理層討論與分析 － 經調整淨收入。

(3) Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of intangible assets (“adjusted EBITDA”), a non-IFRS financial
    measure, eliminates the effect of a number of costs, charges and credits and certain other non-cash charges. Adjusted EBITDA includes
    the lease interest and amortization expense under IFRS 16, Leases (“IFRS 16”) to account for operational rent expenses. We believe these
    measures provide additional information that is useful in gaining a more complete understanding of our operational performance and of
    the underlying trends of our business. See “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations –
    Adjusted EBITDA” for a reconciliation from our profit for the year to adjusted EBITDA.
    未計利息、稅項、折舊及無形資產攤銷前的經調整盈利（「經調整EBITDA」）為非IFRS財務計量工具，其撇除多項成本、費用及貸項以及若干其他
    非現金費用的影響。經調整EBITDA包括IFRS第16號租賃（「IFRS第16號」）項下租賃利息及攤銷開支，以便計入經營租金開支。我們相信該等計
    量工具會提供更多資訊，有利於更全面了解其經營表現及其業務的相關趨勢。有關我們年內溢利與經調整EBITDA的對賬，請參閱「財務狀況及經
    營業績的管理層討論與分析 － 經調整EBITDA」。

    property, plant and equipment and software (“total capital expenditures”) and (ii) principal payments on lease liabilities (each as set forth

Adjusted Free Cash Flow                                                   經調整自由現金流量
We define adjusted free cash flow, a non-IFRS financial measure,          我們對經調整自由現金流量（一項非IFRS財務計
as cash generated from operating activities, less (i) purchases           量工具）的定義為經營活動所得現金減去(i)購置物
of property, plant and equipment and software and (ii) principal          業、廠房及設備以及採購軟件費用及(ii)租賃負債
payments on lease liabilities. We believe adjusted free cash flow         的本金付款。我們認為，經調整自由現金流量可
provides helpful additional information regarding our liquidity and       有效提供有關我們流動資金及能否在不使用若干
our ability to generate cash after excluding the use of cash from         核心經營活動之現金的情況下產生現金的更多資
certain of our core operating activities. Adjusted free cash flow does    訊。經調整自由現金流量不代表可用作酌情支出
not represent the residual cash flow available for discretionary          的剩餘現金流量，原因為其並不包括若干強制性
expenditures since it excludes certain mandatory expenditures,            支出，且經調整自由現金流量的計算可能有別於
and adjusted free cash flow may be calculated differently from, and       其他公司所使用類似命名的計量工具，因此未必
therefore may not be comparable to, similarly titled measures used        可與之進行比較。
by other companies.

(g)   Fair Value of Financial Instruments                                (g)   金融工具之公允價值
      Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an                公允價值是於計量日市場參與者於有秩序
      asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction          交易中出售資產可收取或轉讓負債須支付
      between market participants at the measurement date.                     的價格。IFRS會計準則建立一套公允價值
      IFRS Accounting Standards establish a fair value hierarchy               等級架構，該架構排列用以計量公允價值
      that prioritizes the inputs to valuation techniques used to              的估值方法輸入數據的優先等級。該等級
      measure fair value. The hierarchy gives the highest priority             架構給予於活躍市場中相同資產或負債的
      to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical              未經調整報價最高等級（第一級別計量），
      assets or liabilities (Level 1 measurements) and the lowest              以及涉及重大不可觀察輸入數據的計量最
      priority to measurements involving significant unobservable              低等級（第三級別計量）。公允價值等級架
      inputs (Level 3 measurements). The three levels of the fair              構的三個級別如下：
      value hierarchy are as follows:

      •       Level 1 inputs are quoted prices (unadjusted) in active          •   第一級別輸入數據為本公司有能
              markets for identical assets or liabilities that the                 力於計量日取得的相同資產或負
              Company has the ability to access at the measurement                 債於活躍市場的報價（未經調整）。
              date.

      •       Level 2 inputs are inputs other than quoted prices               •   第二級別輸入數據為不包括第一
              included within Level 1 that are observable for the                  級別的報價的資產或負債的可直
              asset or liability, either directly or indirectly.                   接或間接觀察的輸入數據。


      •       Level 3 inputs are unobservable inputs for the asset or          •   第三級別輸入數據為資產或負債
              liability.                                                           的不可觀察輸入數據。
